newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Boeing sees big 747-400F orders.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sees big 747-400F orders.

text.p: Boeing Co said airlines, especially those in Asia and America, have been showing increased interest in the company's Boeing 747-400F long range freighter.
"I think there will be big orders coming," Boeing marketing vice-president Bruce Dennis told reporters on Wednesday but gave no further details.
Although the 100 tonne plus capacity aircraft cost around $170 million each, they offer significant economic advantages, Dennis added.
On April 16, Flight International reported that the U.S. based Atlas Air cargo carrier is close to deciding on whether to order a fleet of new 747-400s.
It quoted Atlas chairman, Michael Chowdry as saying: "There are some routes, such as transPacific, where the 747-400 freighter's economics make it compare favourably against the 747-200 freighter."

Atlas is the world's largest operator of Boeing 747-200 freighters converted from passenger aircraft with 19 planes wet-leased to top cargo carriers including Lufthansa Cargo, British Airways Plc, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Cargolux and China Airlines.
Under the wet-leasing agreement, the cost of aircraft, crew, maintenance and insurance are charged by Atlas to the companies using the freighters.
Existing 747-400F operators include Cathay Pacific, Singapore Airlines Ltd, Korean Airlines Ltd and its national competitor, Asiana Airlines as well as Cargolux.
